27 Diagrams X and Y show the passage of water waves around an obstacle and through a gap.
The thick lines are barriers to the waves and each thin line represents a wavefront.
X
Y
Which statement is correct?
A
Diagrams X and Y both illustrate diffraction.
B
Diagrams X and Y both illustrate interference.
C
Only diagram X illustrates interference.
D
Only diagram Y illustrates diffraction.

hints: Notice in X the straight wavefronts become curved and enter the shadow region behind the thick barrier, and in Y the straight wavefronts become circular arcs spreading out from the small gap.
Recall that diffraction is the spreading of a wave when it passes an edge, obstacle or aperture of similar size to the wavelength.
Check for interference by looking for two sources whose waves overlap - here each side has only one incident wave train, so look for spreading rather than superposition.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: thick lines are barriers and thin lines are wavefronts. X shows plane waves meeting a single obstacle, Y shows plane waves meeting a barrier with a narrow gap.

State the physical rule: diffraction is the spreading of waves into the geometrical shadow when they pass an obstacle edge or through a gap, with most spreading when gap or obstacle width is similar to wavelength $\lambda$.
Apply to X: the wavefronts to the right of the obstacle are no longer straight across the whole width but curve inward behind the barrier, showing energy spreading around the ends of the obstacle.
Apply to Y: the wavefronts to the right of the gap are concentric circular arcs centred on the gap, showing strong spreading from an aperture comparable to $\lambda$.
Contrast with interference: interference would require two coherent sources and a pattern of overlapping waves, which is not present in either diagram.
Therefore both diagrams illustrate the same effect of spreading by diffraction. This is option A.

A.explanation: Both X with bending into the shadow behind the obstacle and Y with spreading from the narrow gap show diffraction.

B.explanation: Interference needs two coherent sources overlapping to give minima and maxima, but each diagram shows a single set of wavefronts spreading.

C.explanation: Diagram X does not show interference because there is no overlap of two separate wave trains, only bending around one barrier.

D.explanation: Diagram X also shows diffraction as wavefronts curve behind the obstacle, so diffraction is not limited to Y.
